content.jointProblem: Can a content-based or hybrid recommender using product descriptions/category metadata plus session and co-occurrence signals outperform a best-seller list for e-commerce clients with only 500–2,000 completed orders? The collaboration would build and evaluate a prototype for one client, with the first experiment testing whether the researcher's sparse-retail methods transfer to Harmat's catalogue and transaction data.

rationale.text: Erić has a direct doctoral and research focus on hybrid recommendation under data-sparse small-retail conditions.

sources.quote: dissertation on hybrid recommendation strategies for data-sparse retail environments

rationale.text: Her work explicitly combines content-based filtering with behavioural signals from sparse transaction logs typical of SMEs.

sources.quote: combining content-based filtering with behavioural signals derived from sparse transactional logs typical of small and medium retail businesses

rationale.text: She has published on encoding structured product attributes for cold-start item recommendation, matching the company's proposed content-based direction.

sources.quote: structured product attribute data—category hierarchy, price tier, packaging size, and supplier origin—can be encoded into feature vectors to support immediate recommendation of new items

rationale.text: She has tested a hybrid of content similarity and within-session co-occurrence on sparse transactional logs and reported improvement over a pure content baseline.

sources.quote: yielding a precision at three of 0.38 against a pure content baseline of 0.29

rationale.text: She led algorithm development and evaluation in SPAREC, a project aimed at retailers with fewer than five hundred active customers and limited IT infrastructure.

sources.quote: Erić led the work package responsible for algorithm development and evaluation
retailers with fewer than five hundred active customers and limited IT infrastructure

rationale.text: She has analysed when matrix factorization fails under extreme sparsity, which is directly relevant to the company's failed collaborative-filtering attempts.

sources.quote: hit rate drops below the non-personalised popularity baseline at 0.3% density

constraints.text: The method must work with 500–2,000 completed orders per client and cannot assume larger datasets or more traffic.

sources.quote: The largest dataset had 1 900 completed orders over eighteen months; the smallest had around 520.
We do not have the budget or the traffic to wait for larger datasets.

constraints.text: A prototype must be evaluated against best-seller sorting in a client A/B test, not only offline.

sources.quote: Simple best-seller sorting actually outperformed the model in our A/B test on the one client where we got far enough to test.

constraints.text: Content-based or hybrid work needs product metadata complete enough to build attribute vectors; incomplete attributes are a known limitation.

sources.quote: Limitations related to attribute completeness and supplier data availability are discussed.

constraints.text: Data access must be arranged through a data-sharing agreement covering anonymised transaction and product catalogue data.

sources.quote: We can give a collaborator full read access to anonymised transaction and product catalogue data.
access to anonymised client datasets under a data-sharing agreement

constraints.text: The collaboration must fit one mid-level company developer at roughly one day per week and the researcher's caution about more than one day per week outside the faculty during semester.

sources.quote: We can allocate one mid-level developer for roughly one day per week to an applied research collaboration
cautious about commitments that require more than one day per week outside the faculty during the academic semester

constraints.text: The prototype must fit the client e-commerce stack, including PHP/Laravel, MySQL/MariaDB and WooCommerce/REST integrations.

sources.quote: PHP (Laravel framework) for backend portal development
MySQL and MariaDB for transactional data
WooCommerce and custom REST API integrations

risks: Transfer gap: Erić's published evaluations use grocery, clothing, pharmacy, home-goods and other retail datasets, not Harmat's e-commerce clients, so the first experiment must test whether the methods work on one client's catalogue.
The client catalogues may remain too sparse for useful co-occurrence signals; the company already found that the purchase co-occurrence matrix was too sparse to be useful.
Content-based methods can over-specialise recommendations, and product metadata completeness and multilingual description quality are unknown.
Willingness is only confirmed for joint projects; industrial PhD supervision is unknown, and the researcher's availability is unknown and limited during semester.
Harmat has no formal university collaboration experience, and only one mid-level developer at one day per week may be thin for integration and A/B testing.
A one-client A/B test may not give enough traffic for a reliable comparison against the best-seller baseline; success criteria and test duration must be agreed before starting.
questions: Which client and catalogue will be used for the prototype, and what are the exact transaction, user, SKU and time-span counts?
What product metadata fields are available (descriptions, categories, attributes, price tier, supplier), in which languages, and how complete are they?
What is the precise success criterion versus best-seller sorting: metric, minimum lift, evaluation window and available A/B traffic?
Can Harmat confirm the joint-project format, data-sharing agreement, anonymisation procedure and data access mechanism?
What integration constraints apply for the prototype, and who from Harmat will do the PHP/Vue/MySQL/WooCommerce integration work?
Is Branislava Erić available for the required one-day-per-week cadence during the semester, and is there interest in an industrial PhD track, which is currently unknown?
